msContents.summary: Hai ben Sherira's Book of Purchases and Sales (Sefer Meḳaḥ u-Mimkar): in Hebrew

msItem.title: מקח וממכר
Meḳaḥ u-mimkar
msItem.note: The beginning of the manuscript is defective; it currently begins halfway through Chapter 6.

Chapters 8-12 have been edited by Shraga Abramson, alongside two other Hebrew translations and the original text in Arabic, in Jubilee Volume in Honour of Moreinu Hagaon Rabbi Joseph B. Soloveitchik, volume 2 (Jerusalem and New York, 1984), pp. 1312-79, where it is described as the most accurate, though not the most elegant, of the three translations.

The colophon (f. 102v), even under ultra-violet lamp or with infra-red photography, is partly illegible due to the fading of the ink and the staining of the parchment, and has been partly rewritten by a later, Sephardic hand.

The colophon is followed by a partly-illegible poem in the scribal hand. Each line appears to contain one word which either directly refers to, or indirectly puns on, a different personal name; these words have been pointed out either by the scribe or by a later hand. On the side margin, a seventeenth-century Ashkenazic hand had combined the names into a genealogy: חזקיה ברבי אליקים בר יוסף ברבי אורי בן יצחק בר אליעזר בר אלי בנו שלמה גרשם (Ḥezeḳiah berabi Eliaḳim bar Yosef berabi Ori ben Yiẓḥak bar Eliʿezer bar Eli beno Shlomoh Gershom).

supportDesc.foliation: Numbered once every five folios (the numbered folios are ff. 5, 10, 15, etc.).
supportDesc.condition: Ff. 1-2, 101-2 are deeply stained and some of the text has become illegible.

handNote.p: Copied by Gershom ben Shlomoh גרשם בן שלמה , who left a colophon (now barely legible) on f. 102v.

The script is unusual and closely resembles that in Wrocław University Library, Ms. F 46888 (6), which was copied in Münster in 1285; it therefore seems likely that this manuscript was also produced in the German lands during the late-thirteenth century, and Beit-Arié's localisation of the manuscript to Byzantium is almost certainly mistaken.

To mark the end of one chapter and the beginning of the next, the scribe made use of a peculiar graphic symbol (shaped like a reversed letter 's' in double outline; these are used especially consistently from f. 69r onwards) to mark the end of one chapter and the beginning of the next. There are very similar symbols that perform the same function in the 'Birds' Head Haggadah' (Jerusalem, Israel Museum, MS 180/57; Rhineland, c. 1300).

decoDesc.p: A simple micrographical frame and some foliate and abstract penwork decoration (now only partly visible) around the colophon on f. 102v.

Both the style of the foliate penwork decoration and the use of micrography to form simple abstract shapes closely mirror the decorative scheme of the manuscript produced in Münster in 1285, mentioned above (Wrocław University Library, Ms. F 46888 (6)).

bindingDesc.p: Dark brown fine-grained leather over thick wooden boards, with simple blind-tooled decoration on upper and lower boards.
bindingDesc.condition: The manuscript has been rebacked in dark brown fine-grained leather, with the current shelfmark gold-tooled at the base of the spine; the same leather has been used for a few smaller repairs. Two clasps now missing.

origin.note: In the scribal colophon, the date of the completion of the manuscript had faded and was retraced by another hand several centuries later. The retraced date could be either קכז (1366/7) or קפז (1426/7); Beit-Arié has suggested that, due to the absence of superscript marking on the first of these letters in the scribal hand, the original date was probably פז (but for some reason, he derived from this not 1326/7 but 1166/7). On the basis of the resemblance of the script and the decoration to other German manuscripts from the late-thirteenth century, it seems that a reading of the date as כז (1266/7) is the most probable, but this is far from certain.

history.acquisition: It belonged to the library of David Oppenheim (1664-1736), which was purchased by the Bodleian Library in 1829.
